items.context: @XRPathologist (8.129 seguidores), en inglés, respondiendo a tu respuesta sobre drawdowns por ciclo: "I didn't consider that first drawdown due to very, very limited adoption. Most people were clueless to Bitcoin or even how to buy it." Cuenta que ya conversa contigo y aún no le contestas; sigue la conversación con datos de caídas y adopción.
items.suggested_text:
That's a fair reason to set it aside. In 2011 the market was a few thousand early users and one exchange did most of the trading, so a -92.7% move says as much about thin plumbing as it does about holder behavior.

The same logic cuts the other way, though. If thin adoption explains how deep 2011 went, a wider holder base should explain part of why each bottom since has been shallower. Over the last year $BTC fell 32% and the network still added about 2.5M addresses with a balance, something the 2011 market simply couldn't do.

Where it gets less tidy is the recovery clock: the late-2013 high, with a far bigger base than 2011, still took 1,177 days to reclaim versus 622. Adoption seems to cap the depth more clearly than it shortens the wait.
